prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080.

SCENE: A friendly cartoon GIARDIA character - a tiny gut parasite picked up from untreated water - swimming happily in a big simple cartoon mountain stream scene. The Giardia is a plump, rounded teardrop/pear shape, symmetric left-to-right, with a big friendly ROUND FACE: two large round eyes side by side near the top (its real two nuclei), a small cheerful curved smile between them, and rosy cheeks. On its lower front it has one big rounded scalloped fan shape (like a simple sea-shell or a round pleated pocket) sitting on its tummy - its sucker pad - drawn as a closed rounded shape with a few simple pleats/ridges inside, not open, not a hole. From its lower back trail eight long, soft, gently wavy trailing RIBBONS or STREAMERS of even width (like the tails of a kite or ribbon streamers in the wind) - NOT sharp lines, NOT spikes, NOT rays, NOT straight - flowing softly to one side in a relaxed bundle, not spread out evenly all around the body.
Around it in the same scene: a simple wavy line across the lower third of the frame suggesting the stream's water surface with a few simple rounded pebbles poking up; a cheerful cartoon HIKER character off to one side crouched by the stream filling a big rounded water bottle through a simple rounded camping WATER FILTER (a simple cylinder shape with a hose, no small fiddly detail); and a small friendly CAMPFIRE with a round POT bubbling on it further along the bank, steam drawn as a few simple rounded swirl lines (not rays) rising from the pot, showing the water being boiled. Everything drawn large, simple and chunky so a child can colour inside every shape. The mood is playful and reassuring - nobody is sick, nobody looks unwell, nothing unpleasant is shown; the Giardia character itself looks silly and harmless, not scary.

STYLE - coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with generous white space inside them.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN - the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, or a halo/fan of straight or pointed lines radiating out from the body in a circle. The eight tail streamers must be soft, wavy, DIFFERENT LENGTHS, and trail loosely to ONE side like ribbons or kite-tails drifting in water - never fanned out symmetrically all around like spokes or rays, and never drawn as straight sharp lines.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square - the stream water, the bank and the background elements run right off the top, bottom, left and right edges with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO scary face, no sharp teeth, no menacing expression on the Giardia character.
- NOTHING gruesome or unpleasant: no vomit, no sick or distressed faces, no toilet, no bad smell lines, no green clouds, no germs-as-villains imagery.

COMPOSITION FIX from prior attempts that were REJECTED (some had blank white sky/ground gaps, one accidentally added a thin rectangular border line near the edges - both are forbidden): this time, compose the scene ZOOMED IN and LARGE so it naturally fills the square with no deliberate margin anywhere - make the Giardia character noticeably BIGGER, taking up most of the vertical space from near the top edge to the water below, the hiker and campfire scaled up and positioned close to the left and right edges respectively, and the mountain/sky area made much SHORTER (a thin strip only) so the ground and water occupy most of the frame. Because everything is drawn large and close-up, the linework will naturally reach every edge without needing any border, frame or enclosing line - do not add one.
